title: Specify the supplied-design multiplayer transport and authority boundaries
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md, docs/design/SWARM-BRIEF-v0.md, docs/design/RULES-SPEC-v1.md and the listed sourceRefs before editing. The imported Rules Spec v1 is the canonical engine contract; the earlier prototype/T01-T10 interfaces are baseline compatibility, not current gameplay rules. Do not restore approval votes, Repair/Sabotage buttons, Witness or five-node tracks. Preserve original IP and engine independence from Firebase/UI/Node. Edit only ownership; publish APIs only through explicitly owned package entrypoints, preserving baseline exports. Use original synthetic fixtures, scoped tests/lint/typecheck and npm run check. Do not commit, push, open PRs, spawn agents, provision/deploy services, access credentials or alter swarm budget. Write the multiplayer ADR and exact versioned request/reply, persisted room and recipient-view contracts from the supplied design. Distinguish invisible temporary session identity from duplicate-allowed alias and configurable semantic avatar key; no visible account/login. Specify create settings (name,5-10 seats,30/60/90/120 timer,bot-fill/difficulty,visibility,optional passcode hash), host permissions, ready/kick, directory allowlists, deadline generation, request idempotency, revisions, public/private projection and temporary reconnect versus permanent Rules Disconnect. Host requests can advance only after server-checked deadline/phase; local menus cannot pause. Declare provider-independent ports and the D-FIREBASE-PROJECT adapter gate. Use existing baseline canonical IDs/names unless the approved new schema changes them explicitly. Record real source inconsistencies rather than deciding game rules: notably untriggered Ghost Resonance in GDD/ROADMAP versus Rules v1 initial-only ally knowledge, and host-loss/failover details absent from Screen Flow. Do not add a login model, choose unapproved core rules or configure Firebase.
acceptance: The ADR traces every multiplayer setting and authority/privacy invariant to exact supplied source sections, including the invisible identity/alias/avatar distinction.
SERVICE_CONTRACTS fixes versioned lobby/match request, persistence, observer and error shapes, server deadline/revision/idempotency behavior and package boundaries.
The contract separates unconnected transport presence from permanent silent spectator status, hides passcode/hash/hidden authority, and distinguishes host controller from rotating Shift Lead.
Conflicting or missing source behavior is recorded as a narrow explicit decision with references; D-FIREBASE-PROJECT remains external and no SDK/configuration/deployment is introduced.
